HOW TO READ THIS What the curve can and cannot tell you

01 / A MAP, NOT A MEASUREMENT Every point is one curated entry, and a batch release counts once. The curve shows how this collection grows. It is not a measured rate of scientific progress. A selective collection cannot establish a scientific “knee” or an exponential growth rate.

02 / WHY RECENT MONTHS LOOK DENSER Recent announcements are easier to find and still fresh, and older periods have been backfilled by hand. The hero comparison counts entries in two equal 90-day windows ending at the editorial cutoff. More entries can mean more work, more announcements, more attention, or our own selection. It does not prove faster science.

03 / WHAT “BUILDS ON” MEANS A link appears only where the source documents the dependency, for example a model trained on, or using, an earlier system’s outputs. Missing links do not mean independence. Branches in the tree group fields. They do not claim causation.

04 / FOLLOW THE EVIDENCE Each entry links to a primary source and states its limits. Prediction, laboratory evidence, benchmarks and mathematical verification are different kinds of progress. The collection is curated by hand. Automatic updates are not enabled.

ABOUT THIS COLLECTION

Wonder, with receipts.

Intelligence Explosion follows selected milestones in AI-assisted science. Dates mark the linked publication or announcement, not necessarily the first experiment.

Tree branches are subject categories, not claims of causation. “Builds on” links appear only where a source documents the dependency. Points and leaves have equal weight. Their size does not score importance. Every entry comes with its source description and limits.

The collection covers 2020–2026 and is not comprehensive. New findings require editorial review before publication. Last editorial review: .
